payload.title: [bug] Safari login: set Secure + SameSite=None on auth cookie
payload.description:
## What
Safari 17 drops the auth cookie on the redirect from mail.acme-co.com → app.acme-co.com.

## Why
Auth cookie does not set Secure or SameSite=None. WebKit's cross-site cookie rules require both.

## Repro
1. Click magic link in mail.acme-co.com on Safari 17 (private mode, 100% repro).
2. Lands on app.acme-co.com.
3. Bounces back to /login because session cookie is not attached.

## Customers blocked
- Northwind ($200k ARR) — pilot at risk
- Beacon ($90k ARR) — escalated 2026-05-05
- 3+ SMB tickets in #bugs since 2026-05-04

## Acceptance
- [ ] src/auth/redirect.ts sets Secure=true, SameSite=None on the auth cookie.
- [ ] WebKit Playwright test exercising the cross-subdomain redirect added to CI.
- [ ] Verified zero Safari login tickets after 48h in prod.

## Refs
- Slack #bugs root cause: https://acme-co.slack.com/archives/C012ABC34/p1714928400000900
- Auth Architecture Review: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aB3cD4eF_auth_architecture_review
- Feb 2026 postmortem (this regression was already an action item): https://www.notion.so/acme-co/postmortem-safari-feb2026-9f8e7d6c5b4a

payload.title: Implement Safari auth cookie fix + WebKit Playwright test
payload.task:
1) Open src/auth/redirect.ts and update the auth cookie set to include Secure: true, sameSite: 'none'. 2) Create e2e/auth.webkit.spec.ts that simulates a magic-link click on Safari/WebKit, navigates from mail.acme-co.com to app.acme-co.com, and asserts the user lands on /app (not /login). 3) Update playwright.config.ts to include 'webkit' in projects.

Context: Safari 17 drops the auth cookie on cross-subdomain redirect because Secure + SameSite=None are missing. Repro is 100% in Safari private mode. Three customer escalations open.

Do not merge if the WebKit test does not actually exercise a cross-subdomain redirect — that's the regression we're guarding against. The Feb 2026 postmortem already had this as an action item that wasn't completed.

Acceptance: PR open with all three changes, CI green on both WebKit and Chromium projects.

payload.title: [feat] CSV export v2: tuple cursor + NDJSON + column selection (behind flag)
payload.description:
## What
Replace src/api/export/csv.ts with a streaming export that supports:
- Tuple cursor pagination on (created_at, id)
- format=csv | ndjson on the same endpoint
- ?columns=a,b,c whitelist-checked against the export schema

## Why
Northwind ($200k ARR) hard-requires NDJSON. v1 OOMs past ~500k rows. 14 Q1 tickets and 3 sales calls all hit the same gaps.

## Sequencing
Land behind csv_export_v2 feature flag this week. External rollout gated on rate-limit refactor (ENG-2420).

## Acceptance
- [ ] Streaming export for both csv and ndjson, no full-result-in-memory path.
- [ ] Tuple cursor (created_at, id) — not single-column created_at.
- [ ] ?columns= validates against the export schema; unknown columns return 400.
- [ ] csv_export_v2 feature flag gates the new path; default off.
- [ ] Northwind internal demo by 2026-05-30 (QBR).

## Refs
- Spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xK9pP3vL_csv_export_v2_spec
- PRD: https://www.notion.so/acme-co/csv-v2-prd-fedcba654321
- Pattern reference: src/api/orders/list.ts (existing tuple cursor)

payload.title: [infra] Rate-limit middleware → Redis sliding window
payload.description:
## What
Replace the in-process Map in src/middleware/rateLimit.ts with a Redis-backed sliding window (INCR + EXPIRE + atomic Lua check-and-set). RFC approved.

## Why
- We deploy 2-3x/day. Every deploy resets the limiter, so post-deploy traffic is unbounded.
- Local CSV v2 testing already trips the limiter, blocking that work.
- Critical-path blocker for CSV export v2 external launch.

## Decisions already made
- Redis sliding window (rejected: token bucket + Postgres advisory lock).
- Reuse existing acme-cortex-prod Redis instance.
- PR #42 closed; this is a fresh implementation.

## Acceptance
- [ ] src/middleware/rateLimit.ts uses Redis-backed sliding window with atomic check-and-set.
- [ ] Behaviorally identical to v1 from a request perspective (same headers, same 429 shape).
- [ ] rateLimit.test.ts: 'persists across restarts' and 'handles burst correctly' tests pass.
- [ ] Redis memory headroom verified ≥25% before merge (Lin owns).

## Refs
- RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zQ7tR2sN_rate_limit_rfc
- Closed PR #42 (do not reopen): https://github.com/acme-co/cortex-web/pull/42
- Upstash memory headroom alert: 60% peak, monitor.

payload.title: refactor(middleware): rate-limit on Redis sliding window (replaces #42)
payload.body:
## Why
In-process windowed counter resets on every deploy (2-3x/day). Internal CSV v2 testing already tripping limits. Blocks CSV v2 external launch.

## What
- src/middleware/rateLimit.ts: Redis-backed sliding window using INCR + EXPIRE + Lua atomic check-and-set.
- src/middleware/rateLimit.lua: new — atomic 'is this request allowed' script.
- src/middleware/rateLimit.test.ts: replace `it.todo` placeholders with real tests for persistence-across-restart and burst behavior.

## Replaces
Closes #42. Diff in #42 was stale and the test scaffolding wasn't what we wanted.

## Test plan
- [x] Persistence-across-restart test (kill+restart consumer, limit state survives)
- [x] Burst test (101 requests in 1s with 100/s limit → 1 request 429s)
- [ ] Soak test in staging for 24h before flipping in prod

## Refs
RFC: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zQ7tR2sN_rate_limit_rfc

files.patch_summary: replace in-process Map with Redis sliding window via INCR + EXPIRE + Lua
replace it.todo with persistence-across-restart and burst tests

payload.title: Re-implement rate-limit middleware on Redis sliding window
payload.task:
Implement Redis-backed sliding-window rate limiter per the RFC at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zQ7tR2sN_rate_limit_rfc.

1) Rewrite src/middleware/rateLimit.ts to use Redis (INCR + EXPIRE) with a small Lua script for atomicity. Reuse the existing Redis client from src/lib/redis.ts; do not introduce a new dependency.

2) Add src/middleware/rateLimit.lua with the check-and-set logic.

3) In src/middleware/rateLimit.test.ts, replace the existing it.todo placeholders with: a) a test that simulates an instance restart (drop in-process state) and verifies the limiter still enforces correctly, b) a burst test (101 requests in 1s, last one 429s).

Do NOT preserve any of PR #42's diff — that branch is closed because the windowed-counter approach there did not survive restarts.

The limiter's external behavior (request headers, 429 shape, header values like X-RateLimit-Remaining) must be identical to today's. This is the critical-path blocker for CSV export v2 external launch — keep the surface stable.
